summary.text: 右 is the usual character for “right,” including the right hand and the right-hand side. Its older construction is disputed: accounts variously read 又 as a hand, as a sound element, or as an earlier whole sign, and 口 as a mouth, ritual vessel, or later distinguishing mark.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One account treats 又 as a hand and 口 as a ritual prayer vessel, forming a scene associated with ritual service and assistance. Another says 右 began as the whole sign 又 and later acquired 口 to distinguish it. A phonosemantic account assigns 又 a sound role and 口 a meaning role, but the evidence does not settle that analysis or establish the proposed graphic transition.

components.text: One account identifies 又 as a right hand contributing to a ritual scene. Other analyses treat it as an earlier whole sign for 右 or as a phonetic element within the graph; these are distinct claims, and its role remains disputed.

sound_limitation.text: The supplied Baxter–Sagart entries give comparable Old Chinese forms, and both characters have the modern Mandarin reading yòu. These comparisons do not independently establish 又 as a component of 右 or prove a phonetic role.

components.text: The received Shuowen explanation reads 口 as a mouth acting with the hand. A competing account identifies it as a ritual prayer vessel; another treats it as a later mark distinguishing 右 from 又. These analyses assign it different roles.

history.text: Catalogues record forms of 右 across oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, seal, and clerical script traditions. They do not date the cited oracle-bone specimen or establish a precise sequence of graphic changes.

The received Shuowen explanation describes a hand and mouth acting together, and survives in versions that differ in component order. Later commentary and a competing account dispute this as the graph’s original construction; the textual variants do not resolve its formation.

One account proposes that 又 was first used as a whole sign for 右 and that 口 was added later to distinguish the graphs. Another gives 口 a ritual meaning. The supplied evidence does not settle either account or verify the proposed transition.

uncertainties.text: The evidence does not establish which recorded sense came first or a chronological chain connecting direction, assistance, blessing, ritual service, rank, west, and banquet-related use.

A whole-sign borrowing account proposes that 又 was reused to write the word for “right” because of sound similarity. The old object-name and sound match are not independently established here; this proposed borrowing does not by itself show that 又 was a phonetic component inside 右.

senses.gloss: right; right hand or right-hand side
senses.text: The character is recorded for the right hand and right side, but the evidence does not identify either as its earliest sense.
Classical citations record uses meaning help or assist. They are not dated here well enough to establish priority or a development from the directional sense.
Dictionary records include uses for blessing or protection, without establishing their chronology or a semantic link to direction or assistance.
West is recorded as a sense of 右; the evidence does not date it or explain its relation to “right.”
High status or rank is recorded among historical uses, with no chronology or development established here.
A banquet-related use is recorded and glossed as 侑. The evidence does not establish whether this is an extension of meaning or a distinct word written with 右.
The modern political sense is recorded, but no date or account of its development is supplied.

limitations.text: The recorded senses do not establish the earliest Chinese use or a chronological semantic sequence among them.

If 又 was borrowed as a whole sign for a word meaning “right,” the written sign would have been reused because the words sounded alike or similar, not because “also” developed into “right.” The old name and sound match remain unestablished here.

overview.text: 右 is the common character for “right,” including the right hand and right-hand side. Its older construction is disputed: one account sees a hand with a mouth or ritual vessel; another says 口 was added later to distinguish it from 又.

components.text: 又 may depict a hand in a ritual scene; other accounts treat it as the earlier whole sign or as a sound element in 右.
口 is read as a mouth in one traditional account, a ritual vessel in another, or a later distinguishing mark in a competing account.

relationships.text: A competing analysis treats 又 as the depiction of a right hand within a ritual scene in 右.

One analysis assigns 又 a phonetic role in 右. The supplied readings permit a sound comparison, but do not independently confirm the component identity or role; another account treats 又 as an earlier whole sign instead.
One interpretation identifies 口 as a ritual prayer vessel in 右, distinct from the account that reads it as a mouth or a differentiating mark.
A phonosemantic analysis assigns 口 a meaning contribution. The supplied account does not show that this is the same analysis as the ritual-vessel interpretation.
One account describes 口 as a later mark added to distinguish 右 from 又; the proposed graphic transition is not independently verified.
